My meta reflections:

• It feels that the entire economy is replatforming right now.
• Many charts at Stripe are inflecting in quite dramatic ways. What GitHub recently reported for commits we are seeing in economic activity (such as new company formations).
• It is increasingly clear that agents will be responsible for most transactions in the not overly distant future.
• Stripe was always developer-centric, but AI is making developer-centricity strategic in a new way: agents are even hungrier for good DX than developers themselves are.
• Things that we’re launching are increasingly network products at heart. (Instant transfers between Stripe businesses, new kinds of fraud prevention with Stripe Radar, stablecoin payouts to anyone with Link.) "How can we turn Stripe's economies of scale into user benefits?" is increasingly the relevant question.
• Between Privy, Bridge, Tempo, and Stripe’s core capabilities, we’re now doing a lot in stablecoins/crypto, and companies like DoorDash, Ramp, Meta, and Klarna are using our crypto stack to deploy meaningful new functionality in production. “But where’s the production use?” is rapidly becoming stale when applied to crypto.
• After more than a decade of building, we seem to have hit some kind of critical mass of core platform capabilities such that building new things now feels easier and faster than before. (AI also helps.) We've all run into this issue when building with agents: you have to scurry off to establish accounts, clicking things in the browser as though it's the antediluvian days of 2023, in order to unblock its superintelligent progress.

This week's lab covered breadth and depth required for developing AI agent using strands sdk. it covered inbuilt/custom tools usage, MCP usage, memory management, model selection from different model providers such as amazon bedrock, olama; observatibility using langfuse, adding guardrails, etc and finally, providing certification for it https://lnkd.in/eNvaZ3ut. It was long hours of lab but exciting as i completed one example after the other in labs and added more knowledge. What is Strands agent - Its an Open-source SDK for building agents using just a few lines of code . This is something unique from other open source frameworks such as langchain/graph, crewai etc. If you would like to start on Strands agents, here is Git repo with lot of examples in python and other supported languages. https://lnkd.in/exm_4D37 Malashree J D August Innovate • 1K followers 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗩𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗼𝗿 𝗟𝗼𝗰𝗸-𝗜𝗻 𝗶𝗻 𝗮 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗻𝗲𝗿-𝗛𝗲𝗮𝘃𝘆 𝗘𝗰𝗼𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺 “Fintech doesn’t run on one system — it runs on partners.” Banks, payment networks, KYC providers, fraud engines, cloud vendors. Every core capability depends on an external partner. That’s not the problem. Unmanaged dependency is. “Vendor lock-in rarely shows up on day one.” It shows up later: • When pricing changes • When SLAs slip • When regulators demand alternatives • Or when innovation slows because switching is ‘too hard’ At that point, the cost isn’t technical — it’s strategic. “The real challenge is not integration — it’s optionality.” If a partner cannot be replaced without a major rewrite, the platform doesn’t control its own roadmap. And in fintech, that means: • Higher risk • Lower negotiating power • Slower response to regulation and market change “So how do we manage this without over-engineering?” 𝗧𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗹𝗲𝘀: 𝗙𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁: 𝗔𝗯𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗱𝘂𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. Standardize internal APIs so partners sit behind contracts — not inside core logic. 𝗦𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗱: 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘀𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝘂𝗽𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗻𝘁. Even if there’s only one provider today, build as if there will be two tomorrow. 𝗧𝗵𝗶𝗿𝗱: 𝗠𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆 𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗸. Track vendor concentration, failover readiness, and exit cost as first-class metrics. “This isn’t about avoiding partners.” It’s about: • Retaining control • Preserving speed • Protecting long-term margins Well-managed ecosystems scale. Locked-in ecosystems stall. “The takeaway is simple.” In fintech, technology choices become business constraints very quickly. Tech leaders who design for optionality don’t just reduce risk — they future-proof the company’s ability to grow, negotiate, and adapt. JSONLD: {"@context":"http://schema.org","@graph":[{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Anupam Mittal","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/in/anupammittal007"},"datePublished":"2026-10-01T06:10:53.131Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":318},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anupammittal007_you-dont-win-with-a-long-list-of-things-activity-7511306626692349952-WYHH","text":"You don't win with a long list of things to do 🤷🏻

Most plans are just a list of 25 to 50 things to check off.

It feels productive. Tick tick tick. False sense of progress 

In a company or team, usually 1 or 2 bottlenecks are holding everything back.

The job of leadership is simple. 
Find those. 
Put the people, money, and rewards on those. 
Only those.

Everything else is BAU. Business as usual. 
Do it. Don't celebrate it like a breakthrough.

That's how you build OKRs & KPIs. 
80% of the weight on 1 or 2 things that unlock growth.

Rest is just necessary plumbing 😅","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anupammittal007_you-dont-win-with-a-long-list-of-things-activity-7511306626692349952-WYHH"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Anupam Mittal","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/in/anupammittal007"},"datePublished":"2026-09-28T08:21:11.697Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":820},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anupammittal007_is-the-regulator-asking-the-right-question-activity-7510252256538230784-3g9X","text":"Is the Regulator asking the right question?

IRDAI's own paper says premiums grew but coverage did not grow enough.
Costs stayed high over time.

After commissions went into one company cost pot, payouts to distributors grew faster than premium.

So there are two problems. 
Costs are high. 
Coverage is thin.

I am not defending fat commissions 😅
Credit life sold with a loan at high commission is a mess.

But is commission the main reason India is at about 3.7% insurance penetration while the world is near 7%? 
That link is not clearly proven.

If you slash selling incentives before you prove price was the barrier, fewer people will sell. 
Then fewer policies. 
The coverage problem gets worse.

Employment in the industry could also get affected for no obvious & immediate benefit 🤷🏻

Its still early. 
Phase the cut. 
Prove the barrier first.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anupammittal007_is-the-regulator-asking-the-right-question-activity-7510252256538230784-3g9X"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Anupam Mittal","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/in/anupammittal007"},"datePublished":"2026-09-24T11:12:09.408Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":1897},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anupammittal007_anyone-calling-mdr-on-upi-a-tax-is-smoking-activity-7508845729038319617-ChU8","text":"Anyone calling MDR on UPI a tax is smoking something heavy 😅

UPI costs about Rs 20,700 crore a year to run. 
The Budget puts in Rs 2,000 crore of our money. 
Banks and apps eat the rest. 

That is not a free market. That is a subsidised monopoly.

Introducing a low MDR is the right move.
But to keep it that way, we have to ask a deeper question.
Why is there only one NPCI?

In 2020, RBI itself invited rivals.
6 consortiums with serious capital, like TATA & Reliance, applied.
In 2023 the plan was shelved.

Instead we announced a 30% market share cap in 2020.
Still deferred coz 2 apps hold over 85%.

Takeaway👇🏼
You cannot mandate competition. 
You have to enable it.

Telecom had one sarkari operator. 
We opened it up and got some of the cheapest data in the world. 

Visa and Mastercard charge 2% because they are a duopoly. 
Five rails fighting for every merchant cannot.

Enable five NPCIs. 
Kill the subsidy. Let them fight. 
MDR will always stay negligible 🤷🏼‍♂️","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anupammittal007_anyone-calling-mdr-on-upi-a-tax-is-smoking-activity-7508845729038319617-ChU8"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Anupam Mittal","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/in/anupammittal007"},"datePublished":"2026-09-08T10:01:26.662Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":1982},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anupammittal007_indias-biggest-startup-opportunities-often-activity-7503029727822229504-fP5f","text":"India’s biggest startup opportunities often look boring before they look obvious.

UPI did. So did the internet.

At the turn of the century, a marriage broker walked into my father’s office carrying biodatas in a bag.

I remember thinking, how many profiles can one man carry?

The internet was the new rail. Shaadi.com was simply a business built on top of it.

Now another rail is quietly getting built.
Account Aggregator.

Terrible name. Potentially massive opportunity 😅

The RBI-regulated ecosystem has crossed 500 million fulfilled consents, and AA-enabled lending reportedly reached ₹3.82 lakh crore in FY26.

Yet every second pitch I see is still some version of ‘AI for X’.
Nothing wrong with AI.

But we often obsess over the shiny layer and miss the infrastructure changing underneath.

AA could do the same for lending, wealth, insurance, underwriting and financial identity.

The real edge may not always be inventing the future.

Sometimes it is noticing the boring pipe before everyone else sees the water flowing through it 💰","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anupammittal007_indias-biggest-startup-opportunities-often-activity-7503029727822229504-fP5f"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Anupam Mittal","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/in/anupammittal007"},"datePublished":"2026-08-22T05:55:54.973Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":2833},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/anupammittal007_india-mein-sabko-riddhi-chahiye-lekin-activity-7496807345029652480-P0yh","text":"India mein sabko ‘Riddhi’ chahiye ...

A 13-herb hair oil made from a family recipe in their Gurugram kitchen. 

They even drank it on camera to prove a point 🤮
Disgusting, but impressive

2 yrs later, they’re shipping pan-India and doing 30 cr ARR. Crazzzyy ..

My takeaway? 
It all starts with showing up 💪🏼

Riddhi chahiye? Be a Nidhi first
Baaki hum dekh lenge 🦈

A third more revenue. Nearly 3x PAT.

Q1 FY27 Key Numbers:

Revenue: ₹2,714 Cr | +33.6% YoY
EBITDA: ₹589 Cr | 21.7% margin
PAT: ₹228 Cr | +182% YoY

Q1 PAT of ₹228 Cr - compared with ₹530 Cr for the whole of FY26.

The big story this quarter is International. Revenue grew 38%, with EBITDA (pre-IndAS 116) margin crossing 10%. Owndays continues to strengthen in Japan, while Meller’s Paris store is seeing queues daily, with London next. Meller is tracking towards a ~$70M global brand.

And the engine in India keeps getting stronger:
• 0.7 Cr eye tests, up 39.8%
• Roughly 35,000 Indians discover every day at Lenskart that they need vision correction
• 18.3% India SSSG
• 70%+ product margin for the first time
• 80,000+ sign-ups for B by Lenskart, with smart glasses now shipping everyday
• Self-eye testing has entered pilot stores

The last one year has made one thing very clear to me:

We have to build the infrastructure for vision care. You cannot train your way to a billion eye tests. You have to engineer your way there.

AI + eye care + data + smart glasses gives us the opportunity to fundamentally expand access to vision.

Grateful to every customer, every Lenskartian and our shareholders.

Still very early. Still lots to learn.

Still feels like Day Zero!
Q4 and full-year FY26 results are out - our first year as a public company. Grateful to 20,000+ team members across 30+ nationalities who made this possible.

Q4:
• Revenue: +41%
• EBITDA: nearly doubled
• PAT (adj): 2.6x last year
• India same-store sales growth: 24%

FY26:
• Revenue: Rs 9,002 crore (+32%)
• EBITDA: nearly doubled
• PAT (adj): Rs 530 crore - 2.5x last year
• 23.8 million eye tests (+48.5%) - half of them first-time
• 603 new stores added
• Operating Cash Flow: Rs. 887 crore

But this is not the peak.

We are serving 50 million people in a world where billions need better vision. The problem is big and getting bigger - and as we go deeper, the opportunity widens. Smart glasses have opened an entirely new dimension over and above.

And AI has given us wings we have been waiting for.

Every eye test, every transaction, every frame tried on - it all generates data. That data now compounds on itself. Lenskart is no longer just an eyewear company. We are an eyewear + data company.

We're building for the next billion. The best is yet to come.

Detailed Shareholder Letter: https://lnkd.in/g_-YQchq

Grateful
- Peyush","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/peyushbansal_14-years-to-get-here-still-feels-like-day-activity-7462808874144718848-P5AE"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Peyush Bansal","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/in/peyushbansal"},"datePublished":"2026-03-31T18:17:55.724Z","headline":"","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":746},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/peyushbansal_shotonb-activity-7444810225943220226-eg-H","text":"It's past 11 PM on March 31st.
We should probably be asleep, but tonight, we couldn't wait any longer.

We've been working on something for a while now.
Quietly. Nervously, if I'm honest.

Because building glasses is something we know.
Building what comes next - we're still figuring that out.

B by Lenskart is live on early access.

We wanted B to feel like glasses first. Not a gadget. Not a statement. Just a beautiful, comfortable pair of glasses - at 40 grams - with a Sony camera and Snapdragon inside - that happens to carry the future in it.

Hands-free photos and videos. Immersive audio for music and calls. Conversational AI in 40+ languages - still early, honestly, but already surprising us every day. Japanese blue light lenses in every pair.

We have a lot ahead of us - better conversations, better battery, health and nutrition, and so much more we're dreaming about. This is just the beginning.

But here's what matters most to us.
When you buy B, you can walk into any of our 3,000+ stores. Get a real eye test. A real prescription. Talk to a real person who'll make sure your glasses fit and serve you for years. That's not a feature. That's just who we are.

This is one of the most ambitious things we've ever attempted - and an honest invitation to build it together with you.

To everyone who's walked into a Lenskart store, trusted us with their eyes, believed in what we're building -

This one is for you.
We went beyond. Come join us.

👉 https://lnkd.in/gFDxbXwP

META: Founder @WebVeda, @IndiaGeniusChallenge @Monzy • 6X Bestselling Author • 16M+ community · My overarching mission is to empower people to make choices in life from a point of awareness, not ignorance.

Over the past 18 years in the internet and technology space, I’ve had the privilege of working on several ventures - founding some, investing in others, and learning from all. 

Over 16 million people follow my work across social platforms, where I share my experiences and insights on career, mindset, startups, personal finance, and relationships.

Today, my main focus is building my 3 startups

1/ WebVeda.com
A growth platform, offering skills, community and jobs at an annual subscription. 
WebVeda has over 500,000 members as of May 2026

2/ India Genius Challenge
Nation-wide search for the brightest kids in India, through a 2-phase program. 
Winners of the IGC get a Rs. 10L scholarship towards their higher education. 

3/ Monzy.co
The place to find YOUR best credit card.
No ads. No sponsorships. No personal data sought or tracked. 

I’ve also written six bestselling books that have sold 1Mn+ copies worldwide across 63 countries and translated into 17 languages:
- Do Epic Shit (2022)
- Get Epic Shit Done (2023)
- Make Epic Money (2024)
- Build An Epic Career (2025)
- Beyond The Syllabus (2025): for teenagers only
- Winning People Without Losing Yourself (2026)

More often, it’s the small habits around it.
A little less discipline, a little more comparison, a little impatience, and even the biggest goal can remain just that: a goal.

Most ambitious goals don’t fail because they were too ambitious. They fail because the everyday habits needed to support them never quite show up.

Sometimes the best advice makes more sense when you read it backwards.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/riteshagar_ambition-is-rarely-limited-by-the-size-of-activity-7509235042599182336-YqWp"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Ritesh Agarwal","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/in/riteshagar"},"datePublished":"2026-09-23T11:41:47.488Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":934},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/riteshagar_if-you-had-asked-me-a-few-years-ago-how-to-activity-7508490798976376832-Z0A9","text":"If you had asked me a few years ago how to win in life, I would have said work harder.
But my journey taught me something different.

Winning is not about being harsh, loud or ruthless. It's about being clear, consistent and kind even when it's hard.

It's about understanding that no one is going to want your growth as much as you do. You have to show up for yourself every single day.

It's about realizing that your title doesn't define you, your work does. And if you make something with heart, it will always find its way to the right people.

I am still learning, still figuring it out. But these 5 things changed how I look at growth and life.
Sharing it here because I know someone out there needs to hear this today.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/riteshagar_if-you-had-asked-me-a-few-years-ago-how-to-activity-7508490798976376832-Z0A9"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Ritesh Agarwal","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/in/riteshagar"},"datePublished":"2026-09-21T11:24:47.950Z","headline":"","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":658},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/riteshagar_burnout-is-rarely-announced-it-usually-appears-activity-7507761747252899840-4Sck","text":"Burnout is rarely announced. It usually appears gradually in the form of silence, detachment, and a team that no longer feels connected to the outcome.

As a founder, I believe it is my responsibility to notice that shift before exhaustion becomes the accepted way of working. The right numbers help them see beyond the headline growth. Give me a founder who understands the customer deeply, executes with discipline, and can improve a familiar industry year after year. JSONLD: {"@context":"http://schema.org","@graph":[{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Deepinder Goyal","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/in/deepigoyal"},"datePublished":"2026-09-28T08:21:32.595Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":9987},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/deepigoyal_india-has-always-idolised-actors-and-cricketers-activity-7510252344190820352-GlJo","text":"India has always idolised actors and cricketers. The last few years, entrepreneurs and founders have also gotten mobbed at the airports. How I wish we started celebrating scientists as much as we celebrate actors, cricketers, and founders.

On that note, meet the Temple scientists behind Brain Flow: Dr. Divya Gulati (IISc), Dr. Sanchit Gupta (IISc), Dr. Yukti Chopra (SISSA Trieste), and Nitish Kumar (IIT Bombay).

This team led, built, and validated the first continuous, wearable measurement of blood flow to the brain.

Your brain uses 20% of your blood supply. It controls your hormones, sleep, immunity, and repair. That supply drops every year as you age, and you have never measured it. Even hospitals can only capture a single snapshot.

Measuring and maintaining brain flow could be one of the most important health and longevity interventions of our time.

At Temple, we have some of the best minds in the country, working on the one problem that sits upstream of every other: extending healthy human life.

In our second validation study, we tested Temple BrainFlow against time-domain NIRS, one of the few technologies that can separate brain blood volume changes from scalp blood volume changes. We had 60 participants go through three physiological challenges: head-down tilt, stand-to-squat, stand-to-supine.

Across all three challenges, Temple BrainFlow tracked brain blood volume at r=0.84-0.91, significantly more than scalp blood volume. The most significant result came from head-down tilt, where Temple's correlation with the brain was 0.91, and scalp correlation was just 0.49.

Key takeaway: Temple tracks the brain, much more than the scalp.

Why this matters: Cerebral Blood Flow responds to almost everything longevity-oriented people already do. It rises with aerobic exercise, and VO2max correlates directly with it. It rises with cold exposure. It rises with meditation. Better sleep sustains it. It drops when you sit for too long. It drops when you are dehydrated. It is one of the most responsive and integrative biomarkers of how well your body is actually running, and aging.

Until now, you could only measure it in a clinical setting, in a single snapshot. Temple measures it continuously, in real time, while you live your life. And Temple is, as of today, the only wearable in the world with validations against brain blood volume, and not just scalp.

This study was guided by our Scientific Advisor, Prof. David Boas, Director of Boston University's Neurophotonics Center, and the mind behind several new, high-impact, biomedical optical technologies in neuroscience, including NIRS.

This is the second modality Temple BrainFlow is now validated against, after Transcranial Doppler. More coming soon.  Link:  https://lnkd.in/gVwgnWub

The paper is posted as a preprint and submitted for peer review. We encourage researchers to replicate this. We'll happily loan Temples to any qualified researcher who wants to pressure-test any of our metrics independently.

Auto-scroll fired before images loaded — broken animation. Fix: loading overlay until frames are ready + preloaded first frame in <head> + immutable cache headers. 2. Google OAuth Crashing the App Google Sign-In inserted Unicode characters into cookies. Next.js Server Components couldn't parse them — white screen. Fix: edge middleware that sanitizes every cookie value with a regex. 3. signOut() Hanging Forever Browser's Navigator Lock API caused signOut() to hang on some devices. It is great that Nvidia is releasing open source tools for sandboxing AI agents. OpenWorker, our open-source agent harness supporting cybersecurity workflows, is proud to support this.

A sandbox gives an agent limited permissions. OpenWorker is building on Nvidia OpenShell and will support running each agent's commands inside a sandbox. Only the files relevant to the task go in. Secret API keys, your web browser login credentials, the ability to access arbitrary websites, are inaccessible to the agent by default. These restrictions are implemented in deterministic code rather than by prompting an LLM, which can make mistakes or be susceptible to prompt injections. Further, all actions are logged for monitoring and audit.

I'm grateful for Jensen's leadership making AI agents more secure. OpenWorker (which Rohit Prsad and I are working on) will continue to improve security for agents. Mohammed Shoaib is a good example. He started as a support agent, went on to head account opening, and eventually became our head of HR.

been wanting to write this one for a while, Holi break gives that breather. Ishaan Mittal joined our journey back in 2018 when he led the round from Sequoia (now Peak XV) into CarDekho. What followed has been one of the most meaningful investor-founder relationships of my entrepreneurial life.
The startup journey is full of ups and downs. You need people around you who don't just show up for board meetings — they show up when things are hard, and they show up when you least expect it. Ishaan has been that person.
What makes him special is his ability to zoom in and zoom out. He'd dive deep into our receivables data asking for cohort-level analysis one day, and the next he'd share a global product insight from global markets that could reshape our dealer SaaS strategy. He'd question our MIS structure to make it IPO-ready and in the same breath connect us with bankers, partners, and even AI credits to help us move faster. That range is rare in an investor.
He's been a true sounding board. As a founder, you are constantly in dilemma — should I double down or pull back? One of the biggest calls we took was shutting down the used car asset-heavy retail business. That's not an easy decision for any founder. But having a strong board member like Ishaan who brings thought clarity at the right time — that makes all the difference. Honestly, I've avoided a lot of mistakes by getting the right inputs at the right times.
He backs founders. Not just with capital — with conviction, time, and real strategic depth.
As Ishaan embarks on a new journey alongside Tejeshwi and Ashish, I couldn't be more excited. Three exceptional minds joining hands. Really looking forward to what they build together.
Wishing you the very best, Ishaan. Onwards!","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/cardekhoamitjain_have-been-wanting-to-write-this-one-for-a-activity-7434920271591063552-4qHF"},{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Amit Jain","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/in/cardekhoamitjain"},"datePublished":"2026-01-20T08:24:23.547Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":796},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/cardekhoamitjain_revv-cardekhogroup-mobility-activity-7419293707033526272-Qrr5","text":"Turnarounds tell you a lot about people and teams. 

When we partnered with Revv, a self drive car rental platform, it was a tough situation, ₹25 Cr revenue and almost the same amount in losses. Shared mobility that too in b2c space is not an easy business. Capital intensive, operationally complexities and unforgiving if execution slips.

What Anupam Agarwal l and the Revv team have achieved since then is a story of persistence, flawless execution and courage. It is not easy to come out of a downward spiral, but that's what great founders do. They kill what's not working, fix what's right for the long term, innovate and scale with little capital. They say we will live to die another day! That's what Revv team did!! 

In less than 2 years, Revv moved from heavy losses to consistent profitability, scaled nearly 4X and today is running at ₹100+ Cr ARR. Going from -100% PBT to breakeven in under a year and then staying profitable while growing fast, which is very rare. Especially in this sector.

For me, shared mobility has always been more than affordability. It’s about changing how we think about mobility, from ownership to access. Better utilisation, fewer cars, lower emissions and wider access. That belief is what led us to back Revv.

What really worked here was the combination of strong leadership and ecosystem support. At CarDekho Group, we’ve built platforms that help businesses scale faster. Revv leveraged that reach and infrastructure, while Anupam and his team brought deep domain understanding, sharp economics and disciplined execution.

Anupam and team understand the business at a very granular level, like unit economics, customer behaviour, product and operations. The team moved fast, innovated where needed and made hard calls early. That’s how turnarounds actually happen.

This journey has completely validated our decision to partner with Revv. More importantly, it reinforces a belief I hold strongly: great founders with committed teams, backed by the right ecosystem, can make even the hardest businesses work. And this is just the beginning. There’s a lot more to build, new offerings, newer markets and stronger tech, together.

We’re just getting started. Revv and CarDekho Group will continue working on new offerings, new geographies, and stronger tech.

I still remember those early days in Jaipur, working out of a small garage, fueled only by dreams and determination. The easy thing would have been to give up. But we didn’t. We hustled harder, kept our people together, and six months later, we turned things around. That phase taught me that resilience is everything. Fast forward to today— GirnarSoft has grown beyond what we ever imagined. But at the core of all this is our people—the Girnar Family. The incredible team that has believed in this mission and stood by us through thick and thin, and built something truly special. p01_p05.venue: A quiet VIP lounge at the Moscone Center during an AI developer summit in San Francisco
p01_p05.activity: Discussing frontier intelligence ecosystems and building economic infrastructure for AI agents
p01_p05.shared_interest: Frontier intelligence ecosystems and AI-driven workflow transformation

turns.text: Hello Patrick. It's great to connect here in SF. I was just reviewing some of the latest work on frontier intelligence ecosystems, and I think there's a fascinating intersection between what we are doing with Copilot agents and the economic infrastructure Stripe is building for developer-centric solutions.

Hi Satya. Completely agree. The momentum in state-of-the-art collaboration right now is palpable. We're seeing entirely new categories of customer-directed core competencies emerge, particularly as billing and economic infrastructure adapt to autonomous agent workflows.
Patrick has a very clear focus on technical rigor and infrastructure. His perspective on economic primitives for software aligns well with our mission of empowering organizations to achieve more.

Thinking in decades while executing in quarters means we have to get the foundational layers right today. When you look at how work gets done, how do you envision Stripe supporting these multi-agent economic transactions over the next few years?
Satya consistently bridges high-level vision with practical enterprise execution. Discussing API-level integrations for agentic workflows could yield some very compelling joint opportunities.

It comes down to creating technically sound best practices for programmatic commerce. Agents will increasingly need to provision resources, execute micro-transactions, and establish verified partnerships autonomously. We are actively exploring how our developer tools can abstract that complexity.

That resonates deeply. Supercharging everyday workflow isn't just about productivity tools anymore; it's about seamless financial and computational orchestration. We should look at ways our engineering teams can collaborate on these leading-edge solutions.
I would welcome that. Let's set up a deeper dive with our core product leads next week to map out some prospective opportunities and proactive technologies we can tackle together.
Wonderful. Let's make that happen. A positive-sum future is built on exactly these kinds of ecosystem partnerships.
Agreed. Excellent catching up, Satya. I'll have my team coordinate the sync.

decision_a.reason: Strong alignment on enterprise technology strategy, developer ecosystems, and potential avenues for Microsoft-Stripe collaboration.

decision_b.reason: Clear synergy regarding agentic workflows, economic infrastructure, and practical technical execution.

p02_p22.activity: Watching Barça play while discussing AI-driven tactical analysis

turns.text: Hi Andrew! It's great to connect outside of the usual tech conference circuit. I managed to secure some decent seats for the Barça match tonight—figured it was a good way to unwind away from the latest model training runs.

Hi Sundar! Thanks for having me. Honestly, seeing a live match at Camp Nou is incredible. Though knowing us, we'll probably end up debating how computer vision could track player positioning off the ball within the first ten minutes.
